description: Each token is a single centered emblem — a radially symmetric line sigil — floating on a near-black ground with generous margin, reading somewhere between a mandala, a technical schematic and a seal. Construction is stroke-only with no filled areas: an outer carrier shape (a hexagon in seven of the twelve, a plain circle in three, a rotated diamond in one, a dense polygon-star in one), one or two concentric rings inside it, and a small cluster of nested hexagons or rings at the exact center; several tokens add satellite cubes, hexagons or squares orbiting outside the main ring, occasionally clipping the frame edge (10264, 10980). The palette is a strict cool monochrome across all twelve — bone/parchment cream for the brightest carrier line, slate blue-grey for secondary rings, dim mid-grey for the ghosted underlayers — with heavy alpha layering so overlapping members read as translucent lattice rather than solid line. The twelve share the hexagon/circle vocabulary, the six-fold (occasionally four-fold) symmetry, the centered-emblem framing and the three-tone palette; they differ in base polygon, in whether anything orbits outside the ring, and above all in interior density, which ranges from three lonely dots inside a bare circle (9369, 10085) to a woven star lattice packed edge-to-edge with orbiting squares (9548, 9727, 10980). Across the three conditions the same object is rescaled and re-populated: stress contracts the emblem toward the center, dims or outright drops the bright bone carrier ring (9011 loses its entire outer hexagon), pulls satellites inward and thins them out; recovery expands past neutral to the largest and brightest state, restores and multiplies the satellites, and thickens the ring stack into two or three concentric bone outlines — with some elements changing kind, not just count (9190's satellite cubes become skewed elongated prisms, 9548's orbiting squares become open circles under stress).
seenAt120: The silhouette survives cleanly: base polygon (hexagon vs circle vs diamond), the bright bone carrier outline, the presence and rough arrangement of orbiting satellites, and the density class (bare / medium / packed) are all still legible. What is lost is the interior lattice as discrete geometry — in the dense tokens (9548, 9727, 10980) it collapses into a woven texture, and the tiny central clusters become a smudge rather than countable hexagons. The two sparse circular tokens, 9369 and 10085, converge at this size and are hard to tell apart; the hexagon-family tokens stay distinguishable mostly by their satellite arrangement and by how full the interior looks. The scale and brightness swing across conditions would read at this size, since it changes the silhouette's footprint rather than its detail.
